note: Use the supplied graph core as a reference, not a fixed ontology. You may modify, merge, or replace its node and relationship types; document consequential choices and map your representation to the required evidence provenance, tenant/project isolation, source-version identity, assertion state, and human-review state. Equivalent representations are acceptable. Every source must still have an inspectable document representation, even if you rename SourceDocument. Do not treat the listed type names as a checklist.
identity_rule: Graph IDs must be stable and include or derive from tenant/project scope. Source/passage local IDs alone are not global identities.
provenance_rule: Every evidence-bearing assertion and edge must identify one or more configured source passages and retain extraction provenance. Structural or system-generated relationships may have empty source references but must use documented system provenance and remain distinguishable from evidence-bearing relationships.
notes: Document authority/status and assertion authority/status are separate. Preserve historical proposals and later conclusions.
The supplied subject_scope is document-level case metadata, not proof every passage applies to that indication.
Redacted placeholders must remain scoped to the source passage unless an explicit passage establishes identity.
Assay roles may be encoded as edge attributes or explicit role nodes; used_as must have a defined target/role representation. Document the mapping.

Automatically extracted assertions and relationships default to unreviewed. A model call or automated validation is not human review. Keep this independent of the regulatory state reported in the source: an accepted proposal or a reviewer conclusion may still be an unreviewed extraction. Human review and correction are production-design topics only; no working review operation or UI is required. Explain who can review/correct an extraction, what provenance is retained, and how an approved correction would reach indexes and later answers.

Preserve inspectable old source records, assertions/graph exports, and the answers and traces generated before an update, connected by source, snapshot, index and run identifiers. Files are sufficient. No old-version or as-of retrieval/generation interface is required. Current source versions may still describe historical proposals: source revision state and the chronology described by a source are separate.

Source replacement and disagreement between independent sources are different relationships. Preserve both conflicting assertions and their source references when no supported resolution exists. You may add relation/attribute types as needed.
